issues.legal_issue: The land was agricultural tenancy land governed by the applicable tenancy regime.
material_facts: The official record of rights identified the occupant and recorded annual rent for the land.
The land was classified as “Danga Paratan Patit,” meaning high arable land left fallow since olden days.
An objection to the recorded possession had been rejected, and there was no satisfactory evidence to the contrary.
The conveyance to the original owner described a heritable holding on payment of fixed rent, and a later deed also described the land as bearing rent.
issues.conclusion: The land was agricultural land to which the Bengal Tenancy Act applied; the description of it as rent-free land in the earlier sale certificate did not outweigh the other evidence.
issues.legal_principle: A record of rights has presumptive value in the absence of satisfactory evidence to the contrary. The land’s recorded classification, rent, and the nature of the tenure supported treating it as agricultural tenancy land. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.title_possession_suit: A party brought a suit seeking a declaration of title and relief concerning possession of land.
predicates.official_record_shows_arable_land_and_re: An official land record classified the land as arable and recorded rent payable for it.
predicates.satisfactory_contrary_evidence: Evidence was presented that satisfactorily contradicted the official record’s indication that the land was arable and rent-bearing.

issues.definition: When a title-and-possession suit concerns land that an official record identifies as arable and rent-bearing, and no satisfactory contrary evidence is presented, the land is treated as agricultural tenancy land.

issues.legal_issue: A rent-sale purchaser acquired title where the former tenant remained in possession and recorded as representing the holding, while the earlier auction purchaser had not obtained recognition of the tenancy.
material_facts: The land was agricultural tenancy land and the former owner remained in possession after his interest was purchased at an earlier court auction.
The earlier auction purchaser did not have the tenancy mutated into his name in the landlord’s records, while the former owner remained recorded as the occupant.
The landlords obtained a rent decree against the former owner, and the land was sold in execution of that decree to the later purchaser.
The later purchaser obtained possession through the court sale.
issues.conclusion: The landlords were entitled to proceed against the former owner as representing the holding, and the rent-execution auction sale transferred title to the later purchaser.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 13 and 18A of the Bengal Tenancy Act, the landlord was not required to recognize the earlier purchaser as tenant where that purchaser had not obtained mutation of the tenancy in the landlord’s records. The recorded tenant, who remained in possession, could represent the holding in the rent proceeding; the execution sale transferred the interest in the holding to its purchaser. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: rent_recovery_execution_case and land_is_agricultural_tenancy_land and former_tenant_remained_in_possession and former_tenant_remained_recorded and earlier_buyer_failed_to_mutate_tenancy and holding_sold_in_rent_execution

predicates.rent_recovery_execution_case: A landlord pursued recovery of rent from a person recorded as representing the holding, and the holding was sold in execution of the rent decree.
predicates.land_is_agricultural_tenancy_land: The land was agricultural land held under a rent-bearing tenancy.
predicates.former_tenant_remained_in_possession: The former tenant continued to possess the land after an earlier purchaser acquired the former tenant’s interest.
predicates.former_tenant_remained_recorded: The former tenant continued to appear in the landlord’s records as the person representing the holding.
predicates.earlier_buyer_failed_to_mutate_tenancy: The earlier purchaser did not have the tenancy entered in the landlord’s records in that purchaser’s name.
predicates.holding_sold_in_rent_execution: The holding was sold in execution of the rent decree.

issues.definition: When a rent-recovery execution case concerns agricultural tenancy land and the former tenant remains in possession and recorded, an earlier purchaser has not obtained mutation, and the holding is sold in execution, the rent-sale purchaser acquires title to the holding.

issues.legal_issue: A title-and-possession suit is barred where neither the claimant nor the claimant’s predecessor was in possession within the applicable twelve-year period before the suit.
material_facts: The claimant acquired the asserted interest after the later auction purchaser had obtained possession.
Neither the claimant nor the claimant’s predecessor had obtained possession within twelve years before the suit.
The claimant sought a declaration of title and an injunction or, alternatively, possession.
issues.conclusion: The suit was barred by limitation because neither the claimant nor the predecessor in title had been in possession within twelve years before it was filed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the twelve-year limitation period to the claim for title and possession, finding that neither the claimant nor the predecessor had been in possession during that period. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.title_possession_suit: A party brought a suit seeking a declaration of title and relief concerning possession of land.
predicates.neither_claimant_nor_predecessor_in_poss: Neither the claimant nor the claimant’s predecessor was in possession during the applicable period before the suit was filed.

issues.definition: A title-and-possession suit is barred when neither the claimant nor the claimant’s predecessor was in possession during the applicable period before filing.
